title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 7
paragraphs: So when Xerxes had been persuaded to undertake the campaign against Greece, the year after Darius's death he first marched against those who had revolted. Having subdued them and reduced all Egypt to a slavery much harsher than it had suffered under Darius, he entrusted the governorship of it to his own brother Achaemenes, a son of Darius. This Achaemenes, while governing Egypt, was later killed by Inaros son of Psammetichus, a Libyan.
